boundary: slabs and the per-thread object cache
title: Consumer-side defects in memcached's nested allocators: five temporal, three spatial
note: This corpus gitignores its own results/ by policy -- run summaries stay outside it and the case files' status carries the outcome -- so its committed evidence lives in the port named above: capstone-domain spatial/sublet for all five cases plus the negative control, 2026-10-04. Its CheriBSD fixtures also live with the port. Cases 5-7 are SPATIAL, added 2026-10-05 from a SHAPE search over item-size computations (item_make_header / ITEM_* / do_item_alloc) rather than a wording filter -- the wording filter found 0 class-B defects here, and these three have subjects that say 'corruption' rather than 'overflow', which is exactly why it missed them. See docs/ref/memcached-spatial-defect-triage.md. This corpus's .gitignore keeps run summaries OUT of the repository by design -- 'the case files' status carries the outcome' -- so cases 5-7's measured readings live in their status fields and in docs/ref/memcached-spatial-defect-triage.md section 6, not in a committed results/ bundle. 2026-10-07: case 8 is CAUGHT on stock CheriBSD while cases 5-7 complete, and the split is the finding -- src/cheribsd/malloc-leases.c:79 malloc's a slab PAGE which slabs.c then carves, while :161 malloc's each cache OBJECT separately. A slab-chunk crossing therefore stays inside one malloc and a cache-object crossing does not. '0 of 9 caught' would be the wrong summary for this corpus on CheriBSD; it is 0 of 8 and 1 of 1, split by inner allocator.
